issues.title: Ill-defined zero-frequency revised-exit-wave construction

failure_location.quote: Since $\theta(0)$ is undefined, we set $\mathcal{R}_k(\bm{z}_k)_r = \mathcal{F}^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\bm{d}_k}\right)_r$ when $\mathcal{F}(\bm{Q}\odot \bm{z}_k)_r = 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The inverse Fourier transform in the definition requires every entry of the Fourier-phase vector. When the r-th Fourier coefficient is zero, the old footnote leaves its phase undefined and instead assigns the r-th spatial component of the output. Because the inverse transform couples all Fourier entries to all spatial entries, this assignment neither defines the transform nor guarantees the prescribed Fourier magnitudes.
issues.overall_effect: The revised-exit-wave operator, and hence surrogate and gradient constructions using it, are not defined on admissible iterates having zero Fourier coefficients.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the spatial-component fallback with a Fourier-domain phase convention. For y = F(Q⊙z_k), set the phase factor to y_r/|y_r| when y_r is nonzero and to 1 when y_r is zero, form the complete vector sqrt(d_k)⊙phase, and only then apply F^{-1}. Use a consistently specified selector in all surrogate occurrences; classical-gradient claims may carry the standard qualification excluding positive-data zero coefficients at the relevant iterates.
issues.why_classification: Choosing and propagating the missing Fourier phase is genuine mathematical work, so this is not a typo. It is nevertheless a standard exceptional-zero repair, local to the phase selector, that preserves the prescribed magnitudes, objective, surrogate method, conclusions, and rate in the intended regular regime without a new lemma or proof architecture.

issues.title: PIE update lacks a positive-curvature precondition
issues.failure_explanation: The old source permits an arbitrary real vector u. At any coordinate with u=-|Q|^2, the quadratic coefficient vanishes and the displayed update divides by zero. For example, in the scalar case Q=1, d=1, current iterate 2, and u=-1, the surrogate is affine and unbounded, so the advertised argmin does not exist. Strict entrywise positivity of u+|Q|^2 gives positive curvature and a defined quotient.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised generic PIE minimization and explicit update do not define an output for part of their stated input domain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the entrywise hypothesis u_r+|Q_r|^2>0 to the generic PIE formulation and update. Under this condition the quadratic has positive curvature in every coordinate, its minimizer exists uniquely, and the displayed Hadamard quotient is defined; the practical rPIE choice remains covered for a nonzero probe.
issues.why_classification: This is a missing standard curvature precondition rather than a transcription error. The one-line local qualification excludes only invalid regularization choices and leaves the update, method, input regime of practical interest, and all advertised guarantees unchanged.

issues.title: Undefined MG/OPT return value
issues.failure_explanation: The procedure initializes and updates fine-grid variables such as z_h^(j) and z_h^(j+1), but never defines z^recon. Consequently, the printed return statement cannot supply the algorithm's output from its stated variables.
issues.overall_effect: The reviewed MG/OPT procedure has a broken explicit output interface, although its internal iteration remains identifiable.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the undefined return value z^recon by the last computed fine-grid iterate z_h^(j+1), with the index taken from the final completed iteration.
issues.why_classification: The input, initialization, and loop uniquely identify the final fine-grid iterate as the output. Correcting the return variable requires no mathematical inference, construction, or change to the internal iteration.

issues.title: Invalid iterative zero-frequency phase fallback

failure_location.quote: If $\theta(\mathcal{F}\left(\bm{Q}P_k\bm{z}^{(j)}\right)_r)=0$, the original definition is ill-defined

issues.failure_explanation: A nonzero positive-real Fourier coefficient has principal phase zero, so the old trigger can activate even though the original definition is well-defined. Conversely, at an actual zero coefficient the tested phase is itself undefined. The old cases then overwrite a spatial component of the revised exit wave, which neither supplies the missing Fourier phase nor guarantees the phase-recycling identity used in the surrogate analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The iterative surrogate can use an unnecessarily altered or undefined revised exit wave, and the phase-equality step supporting the stated surrogate guarantees is unavailable.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Test whether the Fourier coefficient itself is zero, not whether its phase equals zero. Define its Fourier phase recursively: use the ordinary phase for a nonzero coefficient, use phase 0 for a zero coefficient at j=0, and reuse the previously selected Fourier phase for a zero coefficient at j≥1; then construct the complete revised exit wave with a single inverse Fourier transform.
issues.why_classification: The trigger and fallback operate in the wrong mathematical domains, so more than transcription is involved. The old source already identifies the intended phase-recycling behavior, however, and the corrected local case definition restores the phase identity and all listed surrogate guarantees without weakening them or introducing new proof architecture.

issues.title: False converse in the stationarity claim
issues.failure_explanation: The old theorem claims both directions, while its proof derives only equality of the two objective values implying stationarity. With one scalar scan, Q=1, d=1, and z^(j)=2, the surrogate is minimized at z^(j+1)=1. The new point has zero objective gradient, but the objective decreases from 1/2 to 0, disproving stationarity implying equality.
issues.overall_effect: Only the reverse implication is false; monotone descent and the implication from equality to stationarity remain valid, and the convergence-rate result does not use the converse.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the equivalence by the supported one-way implication Φ(z^(j+1))=Φ(z^(j)) ⇒ ∇Φ(z^(j+1))=0, and remove any prose asserting the converse. Retain the monotone-descent statement and the convergence-rate result unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained and leaves every downstream convergence guarantee intact, so neither global reconstruction nor major loss is required. It nevertheless withdraws a coherent half of the stated equivalence, which is a genuine but limited weakening and therefore exceeds a same-guarantee minor repair.

issues.title: Dimensionally invalid proof of the restriction-product identity
issues.failure_explanation: The statement takes A on the fine grid and B on the coarse grid. The old proof nevertheless writes I_h^H B and I_H^h A, although those products have incompatible dimensions, and its displayed LHS is not the lemma's LHS. The corrected calculation uses B_i(I_h^H A)_i and I_h^H((I_H^h B)⊙A).
issues.overall_effect: The stated identity lacks a valid proof in v1, leaving each later proof that invokes this restriction-product identity unsupported at that step.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the lemma statement and interchange A and B consistently throughout its componentwise proof, beginning with LHS_i=B_i(I_h^H A)_i and computing RHS_i from I_h^H((I_H^h B)⊙A). The existing delta calculation then proves the stated identity, so dependent proofs need no alteration.
issues.why_classification: The declared dimensions and the lemma statement uniquely force a systematic transposition of the two variable names. After that transcriptional correction, the printed algebra is valid without changing any inference, result, or downstream guarantee.

issues.title: Equality does not imply a zero fine-grid gradient
issues.failure_explanation: For positive A, the proof gives minus four times (I_h^H g)^*diag(A)(I_h^H g), so equality implies I_h^H g=0. The restriction has a nontrivial kernel. For example, with one 2-by-2 bin, Q equal to the all-ones vector, zero data, and g=(1,-1,0,0), the surrogate gradient is nonzero while its restriction is zero; the direction and inner product are therefore zero.
issues.overall_effect: The descent inequality remains valid, but its equality case certifies only restricted stationarity rather than full fine-grid stationarity. The later coarse-grid descent theorem uses only the inequality.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the descent inequality but replace the full-stationarity conclusion by restricted stationarity: for entrywise positive A, equality implies, and in fact is equivalent to, I_h^H∇_{z_k}Φ̃_k(z_k';z_k^(j))=0. Do not infer that the fine-grid gradient itself vanishes.
issues.why_classification: The existing quadratic-form calculation supplies a short, contained repair, and the downstream coarse-grid descent result uses only the unaffected inequality. Because restriction has a nontrivial kernel, however, replacing full fine-grid stationarity by restricted stationarity is a meaningful limited weakening rather than a no-loss minor correction.
